events.title: Meadowlark Winter Walk of Lights
events.venue: Meadowlark Botanical Gardens (9750 Meadowlark Gardens Ct)
events.why: A paved half-mile garden loop through animated light displays and lakeside reflections, with s'mores fire pits along the way.

events.title: Downtown DC Holiday Market
events.time: Mon–Fri noon–8 p.m.; Sat–Sun 11 a.m.–8 p.m. (closed Nov. 26 and 30)
events.venue: 1500 block of New Hampshire Ave NW
events.why: The city's big open-air holiday market, with dozens of regional artisans, hot cider, churros and live music.

events.title: Handwork: Contemporary Craft at the Renwick Gallery
events.venue: Smithsonian American Art Museum's Renwick Gallery (1661 Pennsylvania Ave NW)
events.why: A major new craft exhibition of about 50 works arranged around the senses, including dozens of recent acquisitions.

events.title: Takoma Park Farmers Market
events.venue: Laurel Ave
events.why: A car-free street market with local produce, baked goods, warm cider and street musicians.

events.title: Garden of Lights at Brookside Gardens
events.venue: Brookside Gardens (1800 Glenallan Ave)
events.why: More than a million lights along a paved half-mile garden loop, with tickets sold only online in advance.

events.title: ZooLights at the Smithsonian's National Zoo
events.venue: Smithsonian's National Zoo (3001 Connecticut Ave NW)
events.why: DC's signature holiday light show, with glowing animal lanterns, seasonal treats and a zoo train ride.

events.title: Christmas Village in Baltimore
events.venue: West Shore Park, Inner Harbor (501 Light St)
events.price: Free entry; some areas and rides ticketed
events.why: A German-style Christmas market with dozens of wooden huts, mulled wine, bratwurst and a Ferris wheel on the Inner Harbor.

events.title: Season's Greenings: National Parks and Historic Places
events.time: 10 a.m.–5 p.m. daily, closed Dec. 25; until 8 p.m. select Tue/Thu
events.venue: U.S. Botanic Garden
events.why: The holiday poinsettia show and outdoor model trains, with miniature national parks for America's 250th. Warm indoors and stroller friendly.

events.title: Enchant Christmas DC
events.venue: Nationals Park (1500 S Capitol St SE)
events.why: A giant walk-through light maze on the ballfield, with an ice-skating trail and a holiday village.

events.title: Takoma Park Flea and Art Market
events.venue: Seekers Church (276 Carroll St NW)
events.why: A Small Business Saturday edition of this monthly artisan and vintage market a short walk from the Takoma Metro.

events.title: Wegmans Wonderplace
events.venue: National Museum of American History
events.why: Indoor early-childhood gallery for ages 0–6 with play kitchens and crawl space. Pairs with the Botanic Garden.

events.title: Annapolis Grand Illumination
events.venue: Market Space, Historic Downtown
events.why: Live music, ornament making and Santa's arrival at the harborfront tree lighting. Wraps before bedtime.

events.title: 55th Annual Washington Monument Lighting
events.venue: Mount Vernon Place (699 Washington Place)
events.why: Baltimore's holiday kickoff with brass and choir performances, food and cider vendors, and fireworks over the lit monument.

events.title: National Christmas Tree & Pathway of Peace
events.venue: President's Park / The Ellipse (15th & E St NW)
events.why: Walk the Pathway of Peace past trees for every state and territory surrounding the lit National Christmas Tree.

events.title: Heurich House Christmas Markt
events.venue: Heurich House Museum, Dupont Circle
events.why: Juried all-local maker market in a historic mansion garden, with Glühwein. Four days only.

events.title: 9th Annual Mount Rainier Holiday Craft Fair
events.venue: Joe's Movement Emporium (3309 Bunker Hill Rd)
events.why: An indoor Gateway Arts District craft fair with local makers and community performers.

events.title: Alexandria Scottish Christmas Walk Parade & Holiday Boat Parade of Lights
events.time: Walk 10:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m.; boat parade at dusk
events.venue: Old Town Alexandria
events.why: Bagpipers, tartan-clad clans and Scottish terriers parade through Old Town, followed by lighted boats on the Potomac at dusk.

events.title: The Wharf Holiday Boat Parade & Party
events.venue: The Wharf / District Pier (760 Maine Ave SW)
events.why: Dozens of decorated boats cruise the Washington Channel, with live music, kids' crafts and a fireworks finale.

events.title: Yalda Bazar: Winter Solstice
events.venue: Brookland Arts Walk
events.why: 30-plus food and art vendors, a DJ and kids' activities on a paved promenade.

events.title: 44th Annual Eastport Yacht Club Lights Parade
events.venue: Annapolis Harbor & Spa Creek
events.why: Dozens of elaborately lit boats parade through Spa Creek and the harbor, best seen from Eastport's street ends.

events.title: From These Lands at the Natural History Museum
events.venue: National Museum of Natural History, second floor (10th St and Constitution Ave NW)
events.why: More than 600 fossils, minerals and objects, at least one from every state, D.C. and five territories. A free, easy indoor pick for a cold day.

events.title: A Christmas Carol at Ford's Theatre
events.venue: Ford's Theatre (511 10th St NW)
events.why: Ford's yearly Dickens staging, about two hours, in the historic theater. Best for kids 5 and up.

events.title: Dr. Seuss' How The Grinch Stole Christmas! The Musical
events.venue: Imagination Stage, Lerner Family Theatre (4908 Auburn Ave)
events.why: An 85-minute musical made for young audiences, at Bethesda's children's theater. Popular dates price up as they fill.

events.title: National Gallery Sculpture Garden Ice Rink
events.venue: National Gallery of Art Sculpture Garden (7th St and Constitution Ave NW)
events.why: Outdoor skating among the sculptures on the Mall, in back-to-back 45-minute sessions. Open into the evening, weather permitting.

events.title: Christmas Illuminations at Mount Vernon
events.venue: George Washington's Mount Vernon (3200 Mount Vernon Memorial Hwy)
events.why: Two evenings only: the estate lit up for the season with a fireworks show over the mansion to finish.

events.title: Wake Up, Brother Bear!
events.venue: Imagination Stage, Reeve Theatre (4908 Auburn Ave)
events.why: A show built for ages 1 to 4, where kids sit on the floor up close and join in. A good first theater outing.

events.title: Washington Auto Show
events.venue: Walter E. Washington Convention Center (801 Allen Y. Lew Pl NW)
events.price: $15 weekdays, $20 weekends; $7 ages 6–12; 5 and under free
events.why: The region's big new-car show, a full day indoors. Weekday hours are noon to 8 p.m., and floor entry closes an hour before closing.

events.title: Monster Jam
events.venue: Capital One Arena (601 F St NW)
events.why: Monster trucks competing in speed and skill events indoors. Shows Saturday at 1 and 7 p.m. and Sunday at 1 p.m. It gets loud, so bring ear protection for little ones.

events.title: Hanukkah Spectacular
events.venue: Woolly Mammoth Theatre (641 D St NW)
events.why: Woolly's grown-up holiday show, a sharp alternative to the usual Christmas fare. Runs through Dec 13.

events.title: Emily Dickinson Birthday Tribute with Rebecca Lehmann
events.venue: Folger Shakespeare Library (201 East Capitol St SE)
events.why: An hour-long poetry evening at the Folger honoring Dickinson's birthday, led by poet Rebecca Lehmann.

events.title: Daniil Trifonov, piano
events.venue: Music Center at Strathmore (5301 Tuckerman Ln)
events.price: Tickets on Washington Performing Arts' site
events.why: One of the world's top pianists in a recital of Handel, Schubert and Latin American composers.

events.title: DC Improv New Year's Eve Showcase
events.venue: DC Improv (1140 Connecticut Ave NW)
events.price: $35 to $45 early show; $75 to $85 countdown show
events.why: Stand-up to ring in 2027. The 10:15 show ends with a champagne toast at midnight. 18 and over.

events.title: The Axelrod String Quartet: Stradivarius and Amati
events.venue: National Museum of American History, Taubman Hall of Music
events.why: A rare chance to hear the Smithsonian's own Stradivarius and Amati instruments played in concert.

events.title: Hayato Sumino, piano
events.venue: Music Center at Strathmore (5301 Tuckerman Ln)
events.price: Tickets on Washington Performing Arts' site
events.why: The pianist known online as Cateen plays Chopin, Ravel, Saint-Saëns and his own pieces, switching between grand and upright pianos.

events.title: Ten Grand
events.venue: Woolly Mammoth Theatre (641 D St NW)
events.why: A world premiere play by Kate Cortesi at Woolly, DC's home for new and edgy work.

events.title: Seth Parker Woods, cello, with Andrew Rosenblum, piano
events.venue: Sixth & I (600 I St NW)
events.price: Tickets on Washington Performing Arts' site
events.why: An adventurous cellist in the intimate setting of a restored historic synagogue.

events.title: Matthew Whitaker: UPLIFT!
events.venue: Music Center at Strathmore (5301 Tuckerman Ln)
events.price: Tickets on Washington Performing Arts' site
events.why: Jazz and gospel night with pianist Matthew Whitaker, singer Christie Dashiell and youth gospel choirs.

events.title: Seong-Jin Cho, piano
events.venue: Music Center at Strathmore (5301 Tuckerman Ln)
events.price: Tickets on Washington Performing Arts' site
events.why: A recital by the Chopin Competition winner, one of the most sought-after pianists touring now.

events.title: Wordplay Wednesday: Holiday Edition
events.venue: Planet Word (925 13th St NW)
events.why: After-hours word games and holiday fun at the language museum, with the galleries open in the evening.

events.title: Gingerbread Decorating at Gadsby's Tavern
events.venue: Gadsby's Tavern Museum (134 N. Royal St)
events.why: Decorate a gingerbread house inside an 18th-century tavern in Old Town.

events.title: A Very Improv Holiday
events.venue: Studio Theatre (1501 14th St NW)
events.why: Washington Improv Theater's made-up-on-the-spot holiday shows, plus Sunday matinees for families.

events.title: Behind the Science After Hours
events.venue: National Museum of Natural History
events.why: An evening talk at Natural History with a museum scientist on their research. Speaker not yet announced.

events.title: On the Prowl for Winter Waterfowl
events.time: Talk Dec 10, 7 p.m.; field trip Dec 13, 8:30 a.m.
events.venue: Woodend Nature Sanctuary (talk); Gunner's Lake, Germantown (field trip)
events.price: $20 to $28 talk only; $49 to $69 with field trip
events.why: Learn to spot winter ducks at an evening talk, then try it on a guided morning walk at a lake.

events.title: Kids Holiday Needlework at Woodlawn
events.time: 10 a.m. to noon or 1 to 3 p.m.
events.venue: Woodlawn (9000 Richmond Hwy)
events.why: A hands-on holiday stitching class for kids 8 and up in a historic house near Mount Vernon.

events.title: Colonial Handbell Ringers
events.venue: The Lyceum (201 S. Washington St)
events.why: A short free handbell concert in Old Town's historic Lyceum.

events.title: Glenstone
events.time: Thursday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
events.venue: Glenstone (12100 Glen Rd)
events.price: Free; timed tickets required; ages 12 and up
events.why: A huge modern art museum set in rolling meadows and woods, with outdoor sculpture and quiet galleries. Tickets go fast.

events.title: U.S. National Arboretum
events.venue: U.S. National Arboretum (3501 New York Ave NE)
events.why: 446 acres of gardens and trails, including the old Capitol columns standing in a meadow.

events.title: Kenilworth Park & Aquatic Gardens
events.time: Daily, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. in winter
events.venue: Kenilworth Park & Aquatic Gardens (1550 Anacostia Ave NE)
events.why: A hidden marsh and boardwalk on the Anacostia, good for winter birding and a quiet walk.

events.title: Planet Word
events.time: Daily except Tuesday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.; weekends to 6 p.m.
events.venue: Planet Word (925 13th St NW)
events.why: An interactive museum about language, with talking walls, karaoke and a library with secret rooms.

events.title: Library of Congress, Thomas Jefferson Building
events.time: Tuesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
events.venue: Thomas Jefferson Building (10 First St SE)
events.why: One of the most beautiful interiors in DC, with the Main Reading Room overlook and rotating exhibits.

events.title: National Museum of African American History and Culture
events.time: Daily, 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.; Mondays from noon
events.venue: NMAAHC (1400 Constitution Ave NW)
events.why: Plan a few hours. Start at the history galleries downstairs and work your way up.

events.title: Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens
events.time: Tuesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
events.venue: Hillwood (4155 Linnean Ave NW)
events.why: Marjorie Merriweather Post's mansion, full of Fabergé and French art, with formal gardens. Closes for several weeks in January.

events.title: Dumbarton Oaks
events.time: Museum Tuesday to Sunday, 11:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.
events.venue: Dumbarton Oaks (1703 32nd St NW)
events.why: A small, jewel-box museum of Byzantine and pre-Columbian art. The gardens close for January and February.

events.title: The Phillips Collection
events.time: Tuesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
events.venue: The Phillips Collection (1600 21st St NW)
events.why: America's first museum of modern art, home to Renoir's Luncheon of the Boating Party and the Rothko Room.

events.title: Building Stories at the National Building Museum
events.time: Thursday to Monday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
events.venue: National Building Museum (401 F St NW)
events.why: A hands-on gallery where kids build and explore inside the museum's soaring Great Hall.

events.title: Eastern Market Weekend Market
events.time: Saturday and Sunday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
events.venue: Eastern Market (225 7th St SE)
events.why: Farmers, crafts and the flea market around DC's historic public market hall.

events.title: Old Town Alexandria Farmers' Market
events.venue: 100 block of N. Royal St (temporary site)
events.why: One of the oldest continuously running farmers' markets in the country, now at a temporary spot on Royal St.

events.title: Torpedo Factory Art Center
events.venue: Torpedo Factory (105 N. Union St)
events.why: A former torpedo plant on the waterfront, now dozens of open artist studios you can walk through.

events.title: Friday Jazz Night at Westminster Presbyterian
events.venue: Westminster Presbyterian Church (400 I St SW)
events.why: A long-running neighborhood jazz night with live bands and a home-cooked dinner. Very local, very DC.

events.title: Stand-up at the DC Improv
events.time: Most nights; usually dark Monday and Tuesday
events.venue: DC Improv (1140 Connecticut Ave NW)
events.why: DC's main comedy club, with touring headliners on weekends. 18 and over.
